description: Soap is not magic. It attacks the fatty shell of certain viruses and pulls them off your skin. Here is why 20 seconds matter.

hero.hook: A simple weapon against viruses: molecules that love water and love grease.

blocks.text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, one very simple habit moved back to center stage: washing your hands with soap. No laboratory needed. Just water, soap and a little time.
Why does it work so well? Because many dangerous viruses carry an envelope made of fat. And soap is excellent at destroying fat.
Some viruses, such as **coronaviruses** or the flu virus, have an outer envelope made of lipids, meaning fats. That envelope protects them, right up until it meets soap.
Other viruses, called “naked,” have no envelope at all. They stand up better to soap and to alcohol. Luckily, many of the viruses that travel on hands and in droplets are enveloped.

sections.title: The weak point of some viruses

blocks.caption: Scrubbing helps the soap reach every corner of the hands

blocks.text: Soap molecules are [[surfactants]]. They have a head that loves water and a tail that loves fat. The tail buries itself in the greasy envelope of the virus. The head stays turned toward the water.
The result: the envelope tears open. The virus is disabled. Then the water carries the debris away. Soap does not burn the virus the way an acid would: it **dissolves** it and takes it away.
It is the same principle that lifts grease off a frying pan: soap grabs the fat and lets it leave with the water.

sections.title: Soap, a molecule with two faces

blocks.text: The soap needs time to reach every fold: between the fingers, under the nails, around the wrists. About **20 seconds** of scrubbing is the minimum usually recommended.
Without scrubbing, soap works less well. Water alone does not do the job either, since it cannot attack the greasy envelope effectively.

A gel with at least **60%** alcohol can also destroy many enveloped viruses. But if there is visible dirt or grease, the gel works less well, because the dirt gets in the way. In that case, soap and water remain the better choice.
Soap kills many viruses by tearing open their fatty envelope, then washing them away with the water. Time plus scrubbing equals results.
